title: Proxy admission fallback and snowball protection for tenant SLO compliance
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Summary: Implement a proxy-level admission controller that provides graceful fallback and 'snowball protection' during limiter outages and cross-region failover. The controller sits in front of regional throttlers and enforces soft admission windows, spillback policies, and tenant smoothing to prevent cascading retry storms and preserve SLOs for high-priority customers.

Background: We've seen two classes of incidents: 1) local limiter service instability that causes a sharp drop in admission tokens for many tenants, and 2) global retry storms where failed or partially-admitted requests cascade into other regions (the "snowball" effect). Existing limiters are excellent at per-node enforcement but lack a lightweight proxy layer to coordinate temporary backpressure, spillback, and continuum-mode rollbacks while preserving fairness across tenants and regions.

Goals:
- Maintain 99.9% request success SLO for P0 tenants during regional limiter degradations by using proxy admission fallback.
- Limit cross-region spillover such that no single region experiences >15% extra load from spillback in steady-state.
- Prevent retry cascades by introducing exponential admission dampening and a tenant-level smoothing window.
- Provide a safe degraded mode that can route requests to a cheaper/quantized model variant when admission is constrained.

Scope: Proxy admission controller, fallthrough/spillback policies, snowball-protection algorithms, observability (dashboards/alerts), chaos tests, and canary rollout plan. This ticket covers the implementation and staging rollout; follow-ups will hook into dedicated capacity autoscaler and the Console UI for per-tenant tuning.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy admission endpoint accepts and annotates requests with admission_reason and admission_ttl headers
During simulated regional limiter outage (50% token loss), P0 tenant latency SLO remains >= 99.0% vs baseline within 60s after detection
Spillback rate measured as fraction of incoming QPS to secondary regions stays < 15% under steady spike tests
No amplified retry cascade observed in chaos test (total cross-region retries < 1.2x baseline)
Automated playbook triggers with runbook link and one-click toggle to force degraded routing to quantized model variant
decisions: Place admission proxy as a L7 sidecar ahead of regional limiter to avoid changes to existing limiter codebase
Use time-windowed token smoothing (sliding window 10s by default) rather than strict token transfer to bound spillback spikes
Implement a two-stage circuit breaker: fast short-circuit for sudden node failures (5s) and slow degrade path for persistent pressure (120s)
Expose per-tenant weight adjustments via the Console but keep default automatic smoothing enabled
tradeoffs: Sidecar proxy adds ~1-3ms median p99 latency in normal flow; we accept this for stronger cross-region protection
Soft admission increases complexity of debugging — we add verbose tracing and a header-based trace-id propagation to mitigate
Automatic smoothing may underutilize spare capacity briefly to prevent snowballing; customers needing max throughput can opt-out via Console
design_notes: Admission algorithm: maintain per-tenant sliding window counters (10s) and soft credits. If region limiter drops below threshold, proxy reduces admission by dampening factor alpha (start alpha=0.6) and fragments spillback into fixed spill windows (1s granularity).
Circuit breakers: short-circuit when regional limiter heartbeat misses 3 consecutive checks; slow degrade engages when error-rate > 5% for 30s.
Retry damping: tag responses with Retry-After calculated from exponential backoff base=250ms, multiplier=1.8, capped at 5s. Proxy rewrites Retry-After for client-friendliness.
Degraded routing: when admission < 20% for a tenant, route to a lower-resource model variant with preserved schema and cost-verified quality checks.
monitoring_and_alerts: Metrics to add: proxy.admitted_rate, proxy.spilled_rate, proxy.snowball_index (0-1), tenant.smoothing_factor, regional.heartbeat_latency
Dashboards: 'Proxy Admission Overview', per-region 'Spillback Heatmap', per-tenant fairness score
Primary alerts: proxy.spilled_rate > 0.15 sustained 60s (pager), regional.heartbeat_missed_count >= 3 (pager), snowball_index > 0.7 for >2min (pager+slack)
Runbook: link to runbook and one-click degraded routing toggle
testing_plan: Unit tests for token smoothing and spill window mechanics
Integration tests with existing limiter in staging: simulate token loss, increased latency, and 503 patterns
Chaos tests: random limiter restarts, network partitions between proxy and limiter, controlled retry storms to validate snowball protection
Performance tests: measure added tail latency under normal load and at 2x peak load
Canary rollout: 1 region (staging-like) 5% traffic for 6 hours, then 25% for 24 hours, evaluate metrics and rollback if alerts fire
rollout_plan: Merge feature-flagged code behind 'proxy_admission_v1' feature flag
Deploy sidecar to canary region with feature flag on for internal tenants only
Run synthetic and chaos tests for 48 hours; collect fairness_score and p99 latency
Open access to early customers with explicit opt-in in Console; monitor closely
Gradual global rollout with 6-hour observation windows and automated rollback if p0 SLOs drop > 0.5%
risks: Proxy becomes single point of failure if not horizontally scaled — mitigate by single-proxy-per-node and health checks
Misconfiguration of spillback policy could route excessive traffic to secondary regions; add config guards and dry-run mode
Edge cases where degraded model variant fails semantic compatibility — require acceptance tests for model swap
comments: 2025-02-19 Marcus Lin: Initial spike doc posted. Moving to prototype after design sync with infra team. PRD link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/proxy-admission-proto
2025-02-25 Priya Rao (SRE): Reviewed heartbeat thresholds. Suggested reducing short-circuit window to 3s for faster detection; we kept 5s after discussion to reduce false positives.
2025-02-27 Design review - Elena Ortiz: UX for Console toggle looks good; requested an 'opt-out' flow visible in tenant settings. Adding follow-up ticket to Console team.
2025-03-01 Marcus Lin: Prototype sidecar implemented. Initial perf numbers: +1.8ms median, +6ms p99 on small region. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4112

2025-03-03 Load test results: simulated limiter outage with 50% token loss; P0 latency SLO dropped from 99.95% to 99.12% within detection window and recovered to 99.88% after spillback stabilization. Still below target; tuning of alpha and spill window in progress.
2025-03-04 Ava Thompson: Updated acceptance criteria to include explicit Retry-After behavior and degraded routing toggle. Assigned to Marcus for follow-up tuning.
